newsitem.title: USA: H&R Block says CompuServe talks not off.
newsitem.headline: H&R Block says CompuServe talks not off.

text.p: H&R Block Inc, which has been in discussions about a possible business combination for its CompuServe Corp online service subsidiary, said talks have not been discontinued but declined to identify the parties involved.

"Last April, we acknowledged having discussions regarding a possible business combination. There were no assurances that the discussions would result in a transaction," said H&R Block spokeswoman Linda McDougall.

"At no time did we say that the discussions were discontinued and we never identified who we were in discussions with," she said in a telephone interview from H&R Block's headquarters in Kansas City, Mo.
H&R Block owns an 80 percent stake in CompuServe. It spun off about 20 percent of the online information company in April 1996.

The company initially planned to spin off its remaining stake within 12 months, but in August 1996 said it had decided against the option. The company said at the time, however, it believed a separation of H&R Block and CompuServe was in the best interest of its shareholders.

McDougall declined to confirm a report in Monday's Wall Street Journal which identified as possible suitors for the second largest online service Bertelsmann AG, a huge German media conglomerate, and Welsh, Carson, Anderson & Stowe, a New York-based investment firm. Industry sources have also named Virginia-based American Online Inc as a possible buyer.
A Bertelsmann spokesman in New York and an AOL spokesman both said their companies do not comment on market rumors. The spokeswoman for Welsh, Carson, Anderson & Stowe was not available.
Abhishek Gami, an analyst for Nesbitt Burns, said the possible suitors would want the company for different reasons.
"I would be surprised if CompuServe was still an independent company a year from now," Gami said.

He said AOL would be most interested in CompuServe's networking services division, which provides online connections, commerce applications and hosting services for corporations, organizations and other large entities.
Gami said he would expect many U.S. online service subscribers to defect should a merger of AOL/CompuServe services take place.
"There are cultural differences, and there is a significant amount of (subscriber) overlap," Gami said.

Bertelsmann, which owns a five percent stake in AOL, would benefit from CompuServe's large European consumer subscriber base, Gami said. He said as of April 30, CompuServe had about 900,000 subscribers in Europe.
Shares of CompuServe were up 1-3/8 at 12-1/8.
